newsitem.title: MALTA: Business turnover soars at Malta stock exchange.
newsitem.headline: Business turnover soars at Malta stock exchange.

text.p: Turover soared at the Malta Stock Exchange on Wednesday reaching Lm1,067,300 ($2.97 million) in the once weekly session from Lm178,000 ($496,620) the week before.
The share index was up 2.19 to 999.33 with average prices of Mid-Med Bank and Bank of Valletta rising by almost two cents but Farsons shares showing a drop.
There were 151 deals, of which 122 were in equities and 29 in fixed income securities.

Business in equities amounted to Lm 339,280 ($946,591) with 254,130 shares being transacted. Of these, 191,980 were Bank of Valletta shares which were sold in 76 deals for an average of 129.3 cents, up 1.6 cents.
There were 34 deals in Mid-Med Bank, with 55,686 shares selling for an average price of 147.9 cents, up almost two cents.
Ten deals were struck in Lombard Bank Malta at an average of 139.7 cents per share, down from 139.4 when last traded three weeks ago.
A total of 564 Simonds Farsons Cisk Ltd shares changed hands for an average price of 57.8 cents per share, down from 60 cents when last traded on August 28, when they had also lost two cents.
In the government bond market, 14 issues were dealt in, turnover reaching Lm722,283. Business was mainly in the 6.3 percent MGS 1999 (II).
In corporate bonds, there were six deals in the Mid-Med Bank 7.25 percent unsecured loan stock 2005 amounting to Lm5,748.
